package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 and earlier (approximate, as per public reporting)
package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update mechanism was compromised to deliver a malicious backdoor (Sunburst) to customers. The update contained code that enabled attackers to gain persistent, covert access to victim networks, exfiltrate data, and move laterally, affecting government and private sector organizations.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update install)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the Orion service starts or the update is installed), the code delays execution for up to two weeks, then collects system and environment information and sends it to a remote command-and-control (C2) server via HTTP, enabling remote attacker control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is designed to covertly communicate with an external server, delay execution to evade detection, and allow remote command execution, which are hallmarks of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain code that initiates outbound network connections to unknown domains, delays execution for anti-analysis, or executes remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software update checkers may contact vendor servers, but not with delayed, covert, or command-execution logic.
key_indicators: Unusual outbound HTTP requests to non-SolarWinds domains
Long execution delay (sleep) to evade detection
Dynamic code execution based on remote commands

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the SolarWinds Orion update DLL and distributed via official update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of backdoor code on customer systems

attack_chain.action: On installation or service start, the malicious DLL loads and delays execution to avoid detection.
The backdoor collects system and environment data and sends it to the attacker's C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains situational awareness and remote access

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands to the infected system, enabling lateral movement, data theft, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full attacker control and potential data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Delayed execution (sleep for days) after installation or service start
Outbound HTTP requests to suspicious or newly registered domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Unexpected network activity from Orion-related processes
Dynamic code execution based on remote commands
file_indicators: Presence of DLLs with altered digital signatures or hashes
Unusual modifications to Orion update files
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
HTTP POST requests containing system/environment data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion software installations for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to domains not associated with SolarWinds. Analyze DLLs for unauthorized code changes or mismatched hashes. Look for delayed execution patterns and dynamic command execution. Correlate endpoint telemetry with known C2 domains and file indicators.
